source.title: Scaling Laws For Diffusion Transformers
source.authors: Zheng Liang; Hao He; Ce-Yuan Yang; Bo Dai

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling. The text identifies the paper as published at ICLR 2026, although the supplied metadata gives a different venue/year.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law measurements to text-to-image diffusion transformers, rather than testing language-model cross-entropy scaling directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own diffusion-model loss sweeps, compute-optimal allocations, and a large-budget extrapolation. It also reports generation-quality metrics. Results cited from prior scaling-law papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own isoFLOP sweeps (1e17–6e18 FLOPs) on text-to-image diffusion transformers. It fits power laws for loss and for compute-optimal N and D, and checks one extrapolation to 1.5e21 FLOPs. This is a new setting (image diffusion) with results on power-law form (V5), extrapolation (V2), allocation (V3) and fit-dependence (V7). It does not touch language-model loss (V1).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that DiT pretraining loss follows a power law in compute (1e17–6e18 FLOPs). Optimal N and D follow power laws that predicted a 1.5e21-FLOP run. Loss trends match generation quality (FID), even on other datasets. Scaling exponents can serve as a benchmark for model and data design. The limits (text-to-image only, compute-limited regime, fixed hyperparameters) are acknowledged only in the appendix.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an isoFLOP sweep and power-law fitting related to the language-model scaling-law approach, but studies rectified-flow diffusion transformers on image-text data and diffusion training loss rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior or fitted values vary with architecture (In-Context versus Cross-Attention), aspect ratio (mixing 32 and 64 obscures the trend), EMA coefficient (higher coefficients elevate loss values), data captioning (FID exponents differ), and sampling-step count (FID curve offset changes).

fits_no_version.finding: FID, GenEval and human-preference reward scale as power laws with compute. The FID prediction at 1.5e21 FLOPs is said to be accurate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image-generation quality metrics follow compute power laws and can be extrapolated.

fits_no_version.finding: The FID scaling exponent differs between dense captions (-0.234) and sparse tags (-0.216) on the same images.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Caption/data quality changes the generation-quality scaling exponent.

fits_no_version.finding: FID scaling stays linear in log-log for EMA models and across sampling steps. Changing steps mainly shifts the offset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generation-quality scaling form is robust to sampling and EMA settings, which affect only the offset.

record.problems: The main scaling fits use a limited set of compute budgets and a fixed training-hyperparameter setup. The paper notes that the 1e17 isoFLOP parabolic fit is an exception, that more carefully adapted hyperparameters might change fitted curves, and that systematic data-limited scaling remains future work. Many supplementary results are described through figures without numeric values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No results about unrelated formulation ablations or qualitative generated samples were included. Supplementary FID ablations for classifier-free-guidance settings and detailed sampling-step results beyond the stated 35-versus-50 comparison were omitted because they do not measure the listed loss or allocation claims; see Appendix H.1, H.3, and Fig. 8–10.

untested.parts: Entirely untested: no language-model held-out loss is measured.
Only one extrapolation point. No numeric prediction error is reported. No language models.
No language models. It does not test which of the Kaplan or Hoffmann splits holds beyond its own fit. Hyperparameters and the constant learning rate are fixed, not re-tuned per budget.
Depth and width are not swept systematically at fixed N. Only a mixed aspect-ratio figure is given.
No video or other modalities, no fine-tuning, and no systematic repeated-data study (only a single ImageNet data-constrained sweep).
No downstream tasks are tested. The authors state editing and inpainting are not evaluated.
Parameter/FLOP counting conventions, training schedules and fitting methods are not varied.

missing.what: Offset VLB and exact-likelihood scaling curves vs compute, on the training-distribution validation set and on COCO.
FID scaling comparison of cross-attention vs in-context architectures; cross-attention has a steeper slope.
FLOP counting retains context-dependent terms, unlike Kaplan's 6N, because d_model is comparable to context length. This counting choice would affect the allocation fits.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source (Kaplan, Hoffmann) is this paper, so verdicts apply. V2 and V3 are linked only because their wording is not LM-specific; the evidence is diffusion-only. The record's V5 limits_scope (COCO offset) and V7 limits_scope (1e17 parabola) are dropped: an offset preserves the power-law form, and the parabola misfit cannot show bending. The record's 'C^-0.0273' for training loss is EMA-smoothed loss (α=0.9). The extrapolation and many supplementary results are figure-only with no numeric error or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out language-model cross-entropy against parameter count, tokens, or compute, nor the condition that the other quantities are not bottlenecks.
Tests extrapolation of diffusion-model training loss, not language-model held-out loss; the large-budget validation is at 1.5e21 FLOPs.
Tests compute-optimal parameter and data allocation for diffusion transformers, not language models. It does not compare the Kaplan and Hoffmann allocation results directly.
Does not compare depth, width, or architecture details at a fixed parameter count to determine whether loss changes only slightly.

Tests text-to-image diffusion transformers, some image-data settings, and dataset transfer. It does not test video or other non-image modalities, fine-tuning, or transfer of language-model scaling laws.
Does not test downstream-task performance as a function of language-model scale or pretraining loss. Generation-quality metrics are reported separately.
Reports dependence on architecture, aspect ratio, EMA smoothing, and data choice. It does not systematically vary parameter-counting rules, fitting methods, or training schedules.
